insertions.question: Have you tried to size the opportunity at all? Just wondering how you would.

So I'm a little bit worried about the supply chain. The idea that a nursery. The nurseries that I've been to, you throw 100 orders a day at them all of a sudden, and like there's no way they can get that out. They’re just. They function like a mom and pop nursery, and mom and pop are there running the nursery. Do you know what their saturation point would be? Can they handle 100 orders a day? Can they handle?
Each, each wholesale nursery has that capacity right now?
No, I mean for a fulfilment side, it makes sense. But that's still, like if you have one person doing, one person's going to be able to ship what 75 orders a day, if they stood all day and shipped?

Well, yeah, I mean the idea that you're going to all of a sudden spin up 4 new employees in every wholesale nursery, how are you not worried about that? Like, if you don't own that network to do, I mean, you're just hoping these guys can figure it out.

So you mentioned a couple of things that you're doing right now where you've got corporate plants as a service. And then you've got, you've got a retail location, you've got the online ecommerce. You're saying that the direction you want to go is all ecommerce. Do you shut down the retail location? Is that the plan?
Will you expand beyond the one physical location that you have in Brooklyn?
What is, so you acquire me as a customer. How much are you expecting to spend? And then how long until you're making money on me?
So the average order size is one plant? Two plants? What am I?
